description: False-positive and detection gate of the built-in rule file @crs-hardening-conf: every entry records the verdict (block = an interruption, pass = none) at paranoia level 1 with multiphase evaluation, the recommended baseline and the CRS, with the file loaded (expect) and without it (crs_only); rule is the hardening rule that interrupted. The verdicts are measured with the headers the Envoy connector adds to every request (:authority, :path, :method, :scheme, x-forwarded-proto, x-request-id), which the unit test adds as well. benign_groups lists the groups whose requests are ordinary traffic: the file must add no block to them at any paranoia level. Generated from the 2026-11 review corpora; see envoy-coraza/README.md, section CRS hardening supplement.

groups.benign: 84 ordinary requests of the review's benign corpus (6 are blocked by the CRS itself)
groups.header-set: 22 browser and API header sets (none is blocked)
groups.header-matrix: 17 payloads x 4 transports (header, X-Forwarded-Host, cookie, query)
groups.java: 15 Java gadget and serialization cases and 3 URL-safe base64 forms
groups.ordinary: 37 ordinary page, form and API requests
groups.user-agent: 35 browser, library, probe and crawler User-Agent values
groups.header-zoo: 21 realistic header sets of browsers, proxies and clients
groups.encoded-benign: 20 benign values that look like base64 or hex
groups.wrapped: payloads wrapped in base64 or hex
groups.graphql: introspection and ordinary GraphQL requests, single and batched
groups.substitution: command substitutions that print nothing, and prose that resembles them
groups.real-user-agent: 163 User-Agents of browsers, webviews, mobile SDKs, API and CLI clients, cloud SDKs, monitors and crawlers
groups.real-header-set: 116 header sets of browsers, CDNs, proxies, meshes, tracing, webhooks, cloud and auth
groups.native-header: payloads that CRS rules already read in every header (Log4Shell, Shellshock, traversal, Java, PHP open tag), in the headers the supplement leaves alone and others
groups.page-url: follow-up requests of benign pages: the page URL in Referer (25 pages), in HX-Current-URL (25 pages), in X-Original-URL, X-Forwarded-Uri and X-Envoy-Original-Path (3 pages), in X-Original-URI, X-Auth-Request-Redirect, X-Rewrite-URL and X-WAWS-Unencoded-URL (3 pages) and its path in X-Forwarded-Path and Next-Url (4 paths)
groups.type-key: JSON keys and form fields named __type or __schema (Parse Server, ASP.NET AJAX, WCF), which are no GraphQL query
groups.cookie-set: 33 cookie sets: sessions, analytics, consent and auth cookies, some of which hold a URL
groups.password: form and JSON logins with generated passwords that hold $@ or $*
groups.old-client: sec-ch-ua headers of old Chromium releases (GREASE brand with a semicolon) and the Composer User-Agent (10 shapes)
groups.known-false-positive: benign values the file blocks and the CRS alone passes: generated passwords with a pair of backticks, a URL with an IP host in a header or cookie, a field mask, Ansible, a User-Agent that ends in gzip), and base64 of markup (an SVG icon, an HTML snippet, a Gmail raw message)
groups.residue: attacks that pass the CRS and the file: a command in a path segment
groups.upload: JSON bodies that carry random file content, base64 (one line, or wrapped at 76 columns) and hex, 16 to 256 KiB (the CRS alone passes them)
groups.header-class: headers that real clients send: an RFC 7239 Forwarded with an IPv6 client, OData Prefer, copies of Accept-Encoding
groups.ua-command: a command in the User-Agent, bare and behind a Composer shape (the CRS alone passes them)
groups.sink-header: a system file, a command and an internal URL in headers a backend feeds to a file system or a fetcher (X-File-Path, X-Webhook-Url, X-Callback-Uri, ...): the page-URL exclusion lists names, so these are read (the CRS alone passes them)
groups.raw-header-xss: angle-bracket payloads in a header that CRS rule 941100 does not read (the CRS alone passes them)
groups.encoded-value: benign values that the base64, percent-encoding and raw-header rules read: percent-encoded return paths and padded session ids in a cookie, URL-safe tokens, a signature, a PEM certificate, `<` in prose
